chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When you pray over the believer, supplicate for him and strive in supplication.
And if he is standing (in prayer) and is weak (or humble), then magnify (him).
O Allah, forgive those who repented and followed Your path, and protect them from the punishment of the Hellfire.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite when praying over a deceased Muslim according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the act of Salat al-Mayyit is elevated from a mere ritual to an active intercession, emphasizing the necessity of sincere and abundant du'a. The instruction to 'magnify' the status of the deceased, particularly if they were humble or weak, reflects the Shia emphasis on elevating the spiritual standing of the believer through communal prayer. The prescribed supplication directly quotes the Quran, linking the deceased's fate to their repentance and adherence to the divine path.
